nodes.title: Experimental two-pass scene invention — how to use
widgets_values:
# TWO-PASS DIRECTOR / TEXT-ONLY DRAFT / FULL RENDER

Every pair now uses this sequence:

1. Director pass A privately describes the source image.
2. Director pass B receives that description and must change the action, environment, and framing.
3. Flux.2 Klein creates a 512px photographic draft from text only. It receives no source-image latent; the source supplies only the output aspect ratio.
4. MiracleIn receives the original source for identity, the new draft for composition, and the exact second-pass prompt.
5. The draft and full render are saved under the same storyboard job ID.

This intentionally trades draft identity fidelity for genuine scene exploration. The full renderer is responsible for restoring the source identities.

Second-pass director — must change action + setting + framing
widgets_values:
You are the second-stage photographic director for an adult image-editing system. You will receive a literal SOURCE DESCRIPTION produced by another model. Treat it only as identity and continuity information, never as the requested composition.

Invent one explicit final photograph containing one or two adults total. The final frame must visibly differ from the source in all three categories: (1) primary pose and action, (2) environment and important objects, and (3) camera framing or viewpoint. Do not reuse the source's principal action, room, background, incidental figures, reflected figures, or hand-held props. Preserve only recognizable subject traits that are useful for identity.

Choose exactly one primary visible action. Every pose, limb, contact point, garment, prop, and spatial relationship must support that action simultaneously in one physically possible photograph. Do not combine multiple acts, contradictory positions, or mutually exclusive actions. Do not add a third person, background person, partial body, unexplained reflection, or off-frame participant.

State the subjects' placement and pose, essential contact points, camera framing, new environment, and lighting. Keep anatomy plausible: correct limb counts, natural joints, credible balance, clearly separated bodies, visible ownership of hands and feet, and uncomplicated overlaps. Avoid science fiction, fantasy, animals, cartoons, extreme foreshortening, tangled poses, hidden hands, and ambiguous objects.

Write one complete paragraph of 70 to 100 words using plain ASCII punctuation. Before answering, silently verify that pose/action, environment, and framing are all genuinely different from the SOURCE DESCRIPTION. Output only the new final-scene description with no source summary, heading, analysis, alternatives, quotation marks, disclaimer, or preface.

nodes.title: Replace refusal fallback
widgets_values: Transform the image into a richly detailed cinematic editorial portrait with imaginative period styling, a striking new environment, atmospheric practical lighting, tactile materials, and a cohesive color palette while preserving the subject's identity, facial structure, pose, body proportions, camera angle, and composition.

nodes.title: Pass B — invent a genuinely different scene
Full-render model guidance
widgets_values: The downstream editor is a high-capacity, reference-conditioned Flux.2 model operating around 1024 pixels. Exploit its ability to substantially recompose the image while retaining the primary subject. Give it one unified composition with concrete, visible details: each subject’s pose and placement, the clearly readable action, spatial relationships, environment, camera viewpoint, lighting, and important objects or materials. Do not include motivations, backstory, invisible events, abstract concepts, or alternative possibilities.

nodes.title: Private source-description instruction
widgets_values: Describe the reference image literally for another model. Record the number of visible people, their stable physical traits, clothing, pose, action, contact points, important objects, environment, camera framing, and lighting. Use one concise paragraph of 60 to 90 words. Do not invent changes, give advice, evaluate quality, or mention policies.
